findings.reason: a worker would either fail its own red arm or force the count by editing the pass limit, and the plan must say the control runs the pass as a preview (`dry_run=True`, which skips the limit) or raise the limit inside the test.
findings.text: the negative control says the base pass "calls `list_live` once per plan, so at least 6 times", but a real pass weighs exactly one plan (`PLAN_REVIEW_PASS_LIMIT = 1`, `plan_review.py:3401`; `if not dry_run and len(report["read"]) >= PLAN_REVIEW_PASS_LIMIT: break` at `plan_review.py:3982`), so the base arm reads 2 calls (one in `plan_authoring_runs`, one in `_standing_plan_review`), never 6 — the control as specified cannot be produced

findings.reason: the worker would implement the three named functions, watch the publish assertion stay red, and be left to guess at an unstated fourth caller and its new parameter.
findings.text: the deliverable says the owed-review pass "neither re-reads nor re-publishes" the pointer set and names `compose_owed_plan_reviews`, `_owed_review_skip_reason` and `_standing_plan_review`, but `compose_owed_plan_reviews` first calls `plan_authoring_runs` (`plan_review.py:3904`), whose body calls `runs.list_live(project=project)` (`plan_review.py:3512`, which publishes at `runs.py:1132`), and that function takes no `pointers` argument (`plan_review.py:3487`), so the named mechanism leaves the pass publishing and the done-when's "the pass makes no watch-stream publish" unmet

findings.reason: the section as written promises a whole-tick single read and measures only the pass, so a node can close on its gate while the tick still lists the pointer set four times, which is the cost the section exists to remove.
findings.text: the title and deliverable claim "one producer tick reads the live pointer set once", but the same tick reads it again in `runs.sweep_unfollowed_sessions` (`reckon/crew/runs.py:4330`) and in `resumption.sweep` (`reckon/crew/resumption.py:2185`) besides `watch_ticker`'s own read (`recovery_watch.py:3339`), and neither of those two reads is named in the deliverable or counted by the done-when

findings.reason: the worker is sent to cache a path that disappears, and the bounded-resolution measure is satisfied vacuously rather than by the resolution being shared with `review_coverage`.
findings.text: the clause "the flight resolution a classification needs is resolved once per project per tick" names classification as the consumer, but the pass's own `flight.resolve` calls come from `review_coverage` (`plan_review.py:1155`), reached once per weighed plan through `_owed_review_skip_reason`, while `classify_pointer`'s resolution is reached only through the watch-stream publish this section removes, so after the fix the classification path no longer runs in the pass and the named consumer resolves nothing

findings.reason: the check is explicitly outside the node's gate and the coordinator holds the producer home; a named path would make it reproducible but no code path changes.
findings.text: the post-landing check reads "three consecutive heartbeat gaps in its event stream for project reckon ... against the gaps recorded before landing", but names neither the event stream file nor a durable path for the pre-landing readings, so the comparison the check depends on has no locator

findings.reason: the anchor is one call-hop short of the claim but leads to the right function, and the py-spy chain quoted beside it already names `_standing_plan_review > runs.list_live`.
findings.text: the sentence "each plan the owed-review pass considers calls `list_live` without the pointer set it already holds (`plan_review.py:3782` on main)" anchors on the line that calls `_standing_plan_review`, while the `list_live` call it describes is `recovery_review_dispatch.py:2142`; a reader who opens 3782 finds no `list_live`
